name: American Red Cross
description: One of the most recognized humanitarian organizations in the country, responding to disasters big and small every single day.

opportunity.title: Become a Red Cross Volunteer
opportunity.description: Volunteers are the heart of the Red Cross - more than 90% of the workforce is unpaid. You can help families recover after home fires and natural disasters, support blood drives that keep hospitals stocked, teach preparedness in your community, or take on virtual roles like casework and social media from home. Full training is provided, so no experience is needed to start making a real difference.

name: Feeding America
description: The largest hunger-relief organization in the United States, powering a network of more than 200 food banks and 60,000 pantries and meal programs.

opportunity.title: Volunteer at a Local Food Bank
opportunity.description: Hunger exists in every county in America, and food banks rely on volunteers to move millions of pounds of food each week. Through your nearest Feeding America member bank you can sort and box donated groceries, pack weekend meal kits for kids, staff mobile pantries, or help at distribution events. Shifts are flexible, welcoming to groups, and a great way to log service hours with friends.

name: Habitat for Humanity
description: A global nonprofit that has helped more than 46 million people build or improve a place they can call home.

opportunity.title: Build Homes with Habitat
opportunity.description: Habitat brings volunteers and future homeowners together to build affordable housing side by side. On a local build site you might frame walls, paint, or landscape, and no construction experience is required because team leaders teach you everything on site. If swinging a hammer is not your thing, Habitat ReStore resale shops also need help sorting and selling donated goods to fund the mission.

name: Zooniverse
description: The world largest platform for people-powered research, connecting volunteers with real scientists on hundreds of active projects.

opportunity.title: Power Real Research Online
opportunity.description: Zooniverse lets anyone contribute to genuine scientific discovery from a laptop or phone. You might classify distant galaxies, identify animals in trail-camera photos, or transcribe historic weather logs and letters, and your work goes directly to researchers who publish real findings. There is no minimum time commitment, tasks take just minutes each, and projects publish guidance for younger volunteers.

name: Smithsonian Transcription Center
description: The Smithsonian Institution digital volunteer program, opening up the world largest museum and research complex to everyone.

opportunity.title: Transcribe Smithsonian Records
opportunity.description: Behind the Smithsonian are millions of handwritten documents, field notes, diaries, and specimen labels that computers cannot read. As a digital volunteer you turn those images into searchable, accessible text that researchers and the public can use. Work as little or as much as you like from home, pick projects that match your interests from science to history to art, and see your contributions become part of the permanent record.

name: Meals on Wheels America
description: A network of more than 5,000 community programs delivering meals and companionship to homebound seniors nationwide.

opportunity.title: Deliver Meals to Seniors
opportunity.description: For many homebound older adults, a Meals on Wheels volunteer is the only person they see all day. Volunteers deliver hot meals along a local route and take a moment to check in, share a smile, and make sure their neighbor is safe and well. Routes usually take an hour or two, fit around a normal schedule, and the friendly visit means as much as the food.

name: Best Buddies International
description: A nonprofit dedicated to friendship, jobs, and leadership development for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

opportunity.title: Be a Buddy
opportunity.description: Best Buddies pairs volunteers in one-to-one friendships with people who have intellectual and developmental disabilities, and runs school and college chapters across the country. As a buddy you hang out, text, and share activities with your match, building a real friendship that changes both of your lives. Chapters welcome middle and high schoolers, and the e-Buddies program offers an online pen-pal option too.

name: UPchieve
description: A free, on-demand online tutoring nonprofit built for low-income high school students who need academic support after hours.

opportunity.title: Tutor Students Online
opportunity.description: UPchieve connects you with students who often do not have access to private tutoring, right when they are stuck on homework. You get a text notification when a student requests help, hop into a virtual classroom, and work through math, science, or writing one on one, or help with college and financial-aid questions. You set your own availability, there is no minimum commitment, and your hours are tracked so they can count toward service requirements.

name: Learn To Be
description: A nonprofit providing free 1-on-1 online tutoring to underserved K-12 students across the country.

opportunity.title: Tutor a K-12 Student
opportunity.description: Learn To Be matches you with a student who needs steady support in a subject you know well, then gives you the tools and training to help them week after week. Sessions happen in an online classroom on a schedule you set with your student, and consistency is what makes the difference. It is a rewarding way to build a mentoring relationship and rack up meaningful, verifiable service hours.

name: Crisis Text Line
description: A free, confidential, 24/7 mental-health support line staffed by trained volunteer crisis counselors reaching people over text.

opportunity.title: Train as a Crisis Counselor
opportunity.description: Crisis Text Line volunteers support people through anxiety, depression, self-harm, and moments of real crisis, all over text message. You receive around 30 hours of world-class training before ever taking a conversation, and a supervisor backs you up on every shift. This is a serious commitment of roughly 4 hours a week, and it is one of the most meaningful ways to help that exists.

name: Be My Eyes
description: A free app that connects people who are blind or have low vision with sighted volunteers for visual help through live video.

opportunity.title: Lend Your Eyes
opportunity.description: When someone who is blind or low-vision needs a quick pair of eyes, Be My Eyes rings available volunteers around the world, and whoever answers first hops on a short video call. You might read a food label, check an expiration date, describe a photo, or help someone find something they dropped. Calls take just a few minutes, come only when you are free, and millions of volunteers already share the load.

name: Translators without Borders
description: Part of CLEAR Global, a nonprofit closing the language gap in humanitarian and crisis response worldwide.

opportunity.title: Translate for Humanitarian Aid
opportunity.description: When disasters and health crises strike, information has to reach people in a language they actually understand, and that is where this community of volunteer linguists comes in. If you are fluent in more than one language you can translate health guidance, crisis alerts, and education materials for relief organizations operating in over 200 languages. Work is remote and flexible, and every translation can genuinely help keep people safe.

name: UN Online Volunteering
description: The official United Nations platform connecting volunteers with nonprofits and UN agencies for remote work that advances global development.

opportunity.title: Volunteer Online for the UN
opportunity.description: Through the UN Online Volunteering service you can support development organizations anywhere in the world without leaving home. Assignments range from writing and research to graphic design, translation, data analysis, and mentoring, and they plug directly into projects working on poverty, health, education, and human rights. It is a standout way for college-age volunteers to gain real experience while contributing to the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

name: The Trevor Project
description: The leading suicide-prevention and crisis-intervention organization for LGBTQ young people.

opportunity.title: Support LGBTQ Youth
opportunity.description: The Trevor Project provides 24/7 crisis support to LGBTQ young people who may have nowhere else to turn. As a trained digital crisis counselor you support youth over chat and text, and the organization provides thorough training and ongoing supervision before and during your shifts. It is a serious ongoing commitment for adult volunteers, and the impact on a young person in crisis can be life-saving.

name: Ronald McDonald House Charities
description: A nonprofit that keeps families close to their sick children with a home away from home near hospitals worldwide.

opportunity.title: Help Families at RMHC
opportunity.description: When a child is seriously ill, Ronald McDonald House gives their family a warm place to stay just steps from the hospital, and volunteers make that house feel like home. You might cook and serve a family meal, welcome guests at the front desk, organize activities for siblings, or help run fundraising events. Roles and age minimums vary by local chapter, and groups are often welcome.

name: Special Olympics
description: A global movement providing year-round sports training and competition for children and adults with intellectual disabilities.

opportunity.title: Volunteer at Special Olympics
opportunity.description: Special Olympics puts on training and competitions for athletes with intellectual disabilities, and volunteers make every event possible. You can coach a sport, help run competition day, hand out medals, cheer from the sidelines, or support school-based Unified programs where athletes and partners play together. Roles suit all ages, many are one-day commitments, and the energy at these events is unforgettable.

name: Humane Society of the United States
description: The largest animal-protection organization in the country, working to end cruelty to animals everywhere.

opportunity.title: Advocate for Animals
opportunity.description: The Humane Society tackles animal welfare on a national scale, from puppy mills and wildlife protection to farm-animal welfare and disaster rescue. Volunteers power that work through advocacy, phone and text banking for animal-protection laws, event support, and helping spread the word online. If you care about animals and want your voice to influence real policy, this is a flexible way to help.

name: National Park Service
description: The federal agency caring for more than 400 national parks, monuments, and historic sites across America.

opportunity.title: Volunteer in a National Park
opportunity.description: The Volunteers-In-Parks program invites you to help protect the places that belong to all of us. Depending on the park you might maintain trails, restore habitat, greet and guide visitors, assist at a visitor center, or support citizen-science and conservation projects. Opportunities range from a single day of trail work to ongoing seasonal roles, and many parks welcome families and groups.

name: Operation Gratitude
description: A nonprofit that has sent millions of care packages and letters to troops, veterans, and first responders.

opportunity.title: Write to Troops and Veterans
opportunity.description: Operation Gratitude lets anyone say thank you to the people who serve, no matter where you are. The simplest way to help is writing heartfelt letters of appreciation to deployed troops, veterans, and first responders, which get included in care packages shipped nationwide. It is an all-ages activity you can do solo, with a club, or as a family, and every letter genuinely brightens someone day.

name: DoSomething.org
description: One of the largest nonprofits built specifically for young people and social change, with millions of members.

opportunity.title: Join a Youth Campaign
opportunity.description: DoSomething runs volunteer campaigns designed by and for young people on issues like the environment, mental health, education, and equality. Most campaigns can be done right from your phone, whether that is collecting supplies, spreading awareness, or taking a concrete action in your community. Many campaigns also enter you into scholarship drawings, making it a smart way to do good and get rewarded.

name: Girls on the Run
description: A physical-activity based youth development program that builds confidence in girls through the power of running.

opportunity.title: Coach or Cheer with GOTR
opportunity.description: Girls on the Run combines running with lessons that help girls build confidence, kindness, and decision-making skills. Volunteers can coach a team over a season, run alongside a girl as a race-day buddy, or help organize community 5K events. Coaching is the most rewarding role and no running expertise is required, just enthusiasm and a willingness to be a positive role model.

name: iNaturalist
description: A joint initiative of the California Academy of Sciences and National Geographic and one of the most popular nature apps in the world.

opportunity.title: Map Biodiversity
opportunity.description: Every photo you take of a wild plant, animal, or fungus on iNaturalist becomes a data point that scientists use to track biodiversity and climate change. Snap a picture, and the community and its AI help identify the species, adding your observation to a global research database. It turns a walk outside into real citizen science, and it is completely free and beginner-friendly.

name: Tarjimly
description: A nonprofit and app that connects bilingual volunteers with refugees, immigrants, and the aid workers helping them.

opportunity.title: Translate for Refugees
opportunity.description: Language barriers can keep refugees and immigrants from getting medical care, legal help, or safety information. Tarjimly matches you in real time with someone who needs translation in a language you speak, right through the app, for a single conversation at a time. Sessions are short and on-demand, and being fluent in a second language suddenly becomes a way to change someone life.

name: Atlanta Community Food Bank
description: A regional food bank sourcing and distributing food across 29 metro Atlanta and north Georgia counties.

opportunity.title: Sort Food in Atlanta
opportunity.description: The Atlanta Community Food Bank distributes tens of millions of meals a year, and its Product Rescue Center depends on volunteers to make that happen. Volunteers sort, inspect, and box donated groceries so they can go out to partner pantries across metro Atlanta and north Georgia. Shifts are a couple of hours, welcoming to school and club groups, and a great local option for service hours.

name: LifeLine Animal Project
description: The nonprofit that runs metro Atlanta county animal shelters with a mission to end the killing of healthy and treatable pets.

opportunity.title: Help Shelter Animals
opportunity.description: LifeLine operates the Fulton and DeKalb County animal shelters and works to keep them no-kill, which takes a lot of caring hands. Volunteers walk and socialize dogs, spend calming time with cats, help at adoption events, and take photos that help pets find homes faster. It is a rewarding recurring role for local animal lovers, with orientation and training provided.
